theory.summary: Lyrical study in Bb Major (relative major of G Minor) combining rolling arpeggio accompaniment with cantabile melody.
theory.pattern_tip: Bb major shares the exact 2-flat signature of G minor; trace the I-vi-ii-V7-I circle of fifths.
theory.technique_tip: Roll the left-hand 8th/16th arpeggios with supple wrist weight so the Bb-Eb black-key shapes feel effortless.
theory.ballade_link: Trains the warm Bb-major secondary harmony frequently illuminated inside G-minor Romantic works.
theory.concept_title: Bb Major Fluency (Relative Key of Ballade No. 1) & Arpeggio Sweep
concept_paragraphs: Bb Major (two flats: Bb, Eb) is the exact Relative Major sharing G minor's key signature—it appears repeatedly whenever Chopin opens the dark minor curtain onto warm lyrical sunlight.
Notice how the piece uses C7 (V7/V) in Phrase A and B to illuminate F Major (V), while LH broken arpeggios sweep cleanly across two-black-key shapes (Bb and Eb).

form_map.role: Rolling Bb-major arpeggios climbing through Gm (vi) and C7 (V7/V) to F.
Moves through Eb (IV) and Bb/F (I6/4) -> C7 back to Dominant F.
Expands with Bb/D (I6) first inversion for a singing bass counterpoint to F7.
Luminous lyrical closure back onto home Tonic Bb.

practice_steps: 1. Shape LH arpeggios with relaxed wrist rotation—thumbs stay whisper-quiet on beat transitions.
2. Practice I - ii - V7 - vi - V7/V - V in Skeleton mode to hear the bright C7 (E-natural) twist.
3. Bring out the singing RH melody cleanly above rolled accompaniments.
4. Build fluid cantabile motion up to 92 BPM.
